c1-01.title: El manifiesto de Almirante
c1-01.setting: Almirante and Isla Colón, Bocas del Toro, Panama; October 2023 (rainy season), a few months after the 2023 census.
c1-01.logline: Yarisel Archbold, 34, a cargo dispatcher at the Almirante dock and granddaughter of Afro-Antillean banana workers, finds that two cold boxes of insulin and vaccines for the hospital on Isla Colón appear on the ferry manifest but never reached the island, and the port authority wants a name for its incident report by Monday. Every clue points to Lionel Bryan, 68, a stevedore who has worked the dock since the last banana boats and refuses to say where he was during the storm. Yarisel discovers that Lionel, sure the ferry would be cancelled, sent the boxes across on his nephew's water taxi before the storm and never logged it; her report tells the truth without costing him his job, and the dock gets a written storm protocol instead of a culprit.

topics.topic: Impersonal se with people vs pasiva refleja
topics.notes: Choosing between pasiva refleja with things (se cargaron dos neveras), impersonal se + a with people (se citó a los estibadores, no se sancionará a nadie) and ser + participle for official acts. Yarisel's incident report and the inspector's emails contrast things and people. «A las 14:10 se cargaron dos neveras portátiles en la bodega del ferry.» «Se interrogó a los estibadores uno por uno, pero no se encontró a nadie que recordara las neveras.» Also one formal ser passive: «El zarpe fue autorizado por la Capitanía.»

topics.topic: Conditions without si: de + infinitive, de no ser por
topics.notes: Compact counterfactuals: de + (compound) infinitive and de no ser por + noun replacing si-clauses, with the conditional perfect in the main clause. Counterfactuals in the argument about Lionel. «De haber esperado al ferry, la insulina se habría echado a perder.» «De no ser por Lionel, el hospital no habría tenido vacunas esa semana.»

topics.topic: Reporting verbs: negar haber, alegar, admitir
topics.notes: Precise reporting verbs with their constructions: negar/admitir + compound infinitive, alegar/asegurar que + indicative, advertir de que, exigir que + subjunctive. Statements collected for the report. «Lionel negó haber tocado las neveras.» «El capitán alegó que el manifiesto se había firmado antes de la carga.» «La farmacéutica advirtió de que la cadena de frío no admite retrasos.»

topics.topic: Idioms and sayings in dialogue
topics.notes: Fixed expressions and refranes used by characters, with the pragmatic effect each one has in context (warning, consolation, irony). Panamanian dock talk with sayings that carry the moral. «No hay mal que por bien no venga, mija.» «Aquí el juega vivo sale caro.» «Ese informe va a dar mucho que hablar.»

c1-01.register: Formal written (incident report, emails to the Autoridad Marítima) alternating with colloquial dock dialogue; tú among co-workers, usted with the inspector and, at first, with Lionel.
c1-01.dialect: Panamanian Spanish: ustedes, tú; colloquial pela'o (kid), vaina, ¡chuleta! (surprise), chantin (home), juega vivo (cutting corners). Lionel greets in Bocas del Toro Creole English (Guari-guari) once or twice (Wa'appin?), glossed.
idioms: No hay mal que por bien no venga: every cloud has a silver lining
el juega vivo (Panama): cutting corners, gaming the system
dar mucho que hablar: to cause a lot of gossip
tirar la toalla: to give up
c1-01.vocabFocus: Port logistics and incident reporting: el muelle, el manifiesto de carga, la bodega, el estibador, la nevera portátil, la cadena de frío, zarpar, atracar, el zarpe, el taxi acuático, la marea, el oleaje, el aviso de tormenta, el expediente, la sanción, el descargo, el turno, la grúa
facts: Almirante is the mainland port of Bocas del Toro, with ferry and water-taxi links to Isla Colón (Panamanian tourism/transport authority information).

The United Fruit Company (founded 1899) ran banana operations in Bocas del Toro and recruited many Afro-Antillean, largely Jamaican, workers in the late 19th and early 20th centuries (history of Bocas del Toro; academic histories of Afro-Antillean Panama).
Guari-guari is the English-based creole of Bocas del Toro (linguistic descriptions of Panamanian creoles).
Panama's 2010 census was the first to ask about Afro-descendant self-identification (9.2%); the 2023 census recorded 31.7% (INEC Panamá; UN Working Group report).

roleplay.goal: Get Lionel to tell you what he did during the storm without accusing him, and persuade him to sign a short statement for the report.
roleplay.register: usted with an older man, moving to tú when he invites it; colloquial Panamanian

c1-01.scene: Rainy dusk on the Almirante dock: Yarisel in a hi-vis vest with a tablet, Lionel in a yellow rain jacket beside a small blue water taxi, two white cold boxes with red-cross stickers, the car ferry blurred behind. Slate-grey sky, turquoise water, yellow and red accents.
canDo: C1-S2: I can ask someone tactfully about a sensitive matter, adapting register (tú, usted, vos) to the person and the situation.
C1-R1: I can follow a long story with several timelines and embedded documents (reports, ledgers, wills, scripts) and say what is established and what is only inferred.

c1-02.title: Lo que silbó el barranco
c1-02.setting: Chipude and Valle Gran Rey, La Gomera (Canary Islands, Spain); April, present day.
c1-02.logline: Íñigo Saldaña, 31, a food journalist from Madrid, is on the jury of a goat-cheese contest in Chipude when the favourite cheese disappears from a locked room an hour before the verdict. The only witness is a whistled message that crossed the ravine at the moment of the theft, and the islanders who understand silbo gomero, including retired teacher Chano Darias, 66, won't translate it for an outsider. Íñigo learns enough silbo to decode it: the cheesemaker Yurena Chinea removed her own cheese because it was made partly with milk from her rival Ayoze's herd after her goats fell ill, and the whistle was Chano telling her to bring it back and say so, so the jury ends up giving the two herds a joint mention.

topics.topic: Cause and consequence: de ahí que, no porque… sino porque
topics.notes: de ahí que + subjunctive (the consequence is presented as known) and the rejected cause no porque + subjunctive… sino porque + indicative. The jury's reasoning and Íñigo's article. «El queso estaba bajo llave; de ahí que nadie entendiera cómo había desaparecido.» «No lo retiró porque fuera malo, sino porque no era del todo suyo.»

topics.topic: Formal relatives: el cual, lo cual
topics.notes: el cual / la cual after longer or compound prepositions (desde el cual, a raíz de la cual) and lo cual referring back to a whole clause; B2 already covered en el que and cuyo. Íñigo's literary-journalistic prose. «Chano me llevó al mirador, desde el cual se oía todo el barranco.» «Yurena no se presentó a la cata, lo cual levantó sospechas.»

topics.topic: Pseudo-clefts: lo que pasó fue que
topics.notes: lo que / lo único que / quien … + ser to put the new information at the end (lo que me molesta es…, lo que pasó fue que…); B2 covered fue X quien. Focus on what really matters in the mystery. «Lo que nadie me había dicho era que el barranco también escucha.» «Lo único que pido es que alguien me traduzca ese silbido.»

topics.topic: Idioms and sayings in dialogue
topics.notes: Fixed expressions and refranes used by characters, with the pragmatic effect each one has in context (warning, consolation, irony). Island sayings used against and by the outsider. «A buen entendedor, pocas palabras bastan, y aquí ni palabras hacen falta.» «Pueblo chico, infierno grande.» «Aquí nadie da gato por liebre.»

c1-02.register: Íñigo's polished first-person journalism and his Madrid colloquial with vosotros; islanders' informal Canarian speech; the jury's formal announcements.
c1-02.dialect: Canarian Spanish: ustedes as the only plural 'you' (contrast with Íñigo's vosotros), seseo, papas, guagua, millo, mi niño. Silbo gomero rendered as whistled vowels and consonant classes described in the narration.
idioms: A buen entendedor, pocas palabras bastan: a word to the wise is enough
Pueblo chico, infierno grande: in a small town everyone knows your business
dar gato por liebre: to pass off something inferior as the real thing
no dar su brazo a torcer: to refuse to back down
c1-02.vocabFocus: Island landscape and cheese-making: el silbo, el barranco, la ladera, el bancal, el mirador, el eco, el queso de cabra, la cuajada, el suero, el rebaño, el cabrero, el jurado, la cata, la corteza, el almogrote, el ahumado, el certamen, la descalificación
facts: Silbo gomero was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009 (UNESCO ICH, element 00172).

Silbo has been taught in La Gomera's schools since 1999 as part of the curriculum (UNESCO ICH page; Canarian press). Do not call it 'compulsory by law' without checking the Canarian education regulation.
Silbo transposes spoken Spanish into whistled pitch contrasts for vowels and consonant groups (phonetic studies of silbo gomero).
Almogrote is a Gomeran spread of aged goat cheese, pepper and oil (Canarian gastronomy guides).

roleplay.goal: Convince Chano to help you understand the whistled message, showing you respect the tradition and are not just after a story.
roleplay.register: usted with an older islander; he answers with Canarian ustedes and humour

c1-02.scene: Terraced green ravine on La Gomera with Teide on the horizon across the sea; an older man whistling with a finger in his mouth at a stone viewpoint, a young man in a city jacket with a notebook, a table of goat cheeses under a white cloth with one empty plate. Ochre, terrace green, Atlantic blue.
canDo: C1-S3: I can give a reasoned explanation of a problem and its causes, conceding points and arguing back (si bien…, aun así, de ahí que…).
C1-R4: I can understand idioms, sayings and cultural references in context, including terms from Afro-Latin traditions (marimba de chonta, Garífuna, liberto, Danza de los Diablos).

c1-03.title: La marimba que no quería sonar
c1-03.setting: Buenaventura and Cali (Valle del Cauca), Colombia; August, the week of the Petronio Álvarez Festival, present day.
c1-03.logline: Nayibe Angulo, 29, an acoustic engineer in Cali, delivers the marimba de chonta that her grandfather Celestino, 74, a marimba maker from Guapi who works in Buenaventura, built for a group in the Petronio Álvarez final. In Cali the marimba suddenly sounds sour, and the group's director, Gerardo Riascos, is sure a rival tampered with it two days before the competition. Nayibe's electronic tuner and her grandfather's ear disagree until she realises the chonta keys have dried out in Cali's air after the humidity of Buenaventura; she retunes them overnight her grandfather's way and finally understands why he insists a marimba must rest in the city before a festival.

topics.topic: Present perfect subjunctive: haya + participle
topics.notes: First headline for haya + participle (absent at B1/B2): past or completed events seen from a present that requires the subjunctive (no creo que, me alegra que, cuando + future completion). Doubts and future completions about the instrument. «No creo que nadie la haya tocado; los tubos están como los dejé.» «Cuando hayas afinado la última tecla, me llamas, mija.»

topics.topic: Concessives beyond aunque: si bien, aun cuando, por más que
topics.notes: si bien (+ indicative, formal), aun cuando and a pesar de que (indicative = fact; subjunctive = possibility or conceded point), por más que (+ subjunctive or indicative). Engineer versus elder. «Si bien el afinador marcaba un la perfecto, a mi abuelo le sonaba agrio.» «Por más que se lo expliqué, Gerardo no aceptaba que fuera el clima.» «Aun cuando ganemos, esta marimba vuelve a Buenaventura el lunes.»

topics.topic: Future perfect: completion and conjecture
topics.notes: habrá + participle for completion before a future point (para el viernes habrá secado) and for guesses about the past (¿quién habrá abierto la caja?); B2 had only the conditional perfect. Deadlines and guesses. «Para el viernes ya se habrá secado la chonta.» «¿Quién habrá abierto la caja en el bus?»

c1-03.register: Colloquial family dialogue (Colombian usted de confianza between grandfather and granddaughter), Nayibe's technical notes, the festival's formal announcements.
c1-03.dialect: Colombian Pacific Spanish: usted among intimates, ustedes, ¡ajá!, ¿qué hubo?, mija, mi pariente; s-aspiration noted for the audio. Instrument names: cununo, bombo, guasá; cantaora.
idioms: Despacio que voy de afán: more haste, less speed
dar papaya (Colombia): to give someone an easy opportunity to take advantage
estar en las mismas: to be back where you started
al que no le gusta el caldo, le dan dos tazas: you get more of what you complain about
c1-03.vocabFocus: Instrument-making and performance: la marimba de chonta, la tecla, el tubo de guadua, el resonador, el cununo, el bombo, el guasá, la cantaora, afinar, desafinado, la humedad, la tarima, el ensayo, el jurado, el arrullo, el currulao, lijar, el afinador, la frecuencia
facts: The Festival de Música del Pacífico Petronio Álvarez has been held in Cali since 1997 (Alcaldía de Cali; some outlets date the first call to 1996).
Its categories are marimba, chirimía, violines caucanos (added in 2008) and agrupación libre (Alcaldía de Cali).
'Marimba music and traditional chants from Colombia's South Pacific region' was inscribed by UNESCO in 2010 and extended in 2015 to include Esmeraldas Province, Ecuador (UNESCO ICH list).
The marimba de chonta has keys of chonta palm wood and guadua bamboo resonators (organology of the Pacific marimba).
Petronio Álvarez was a Buenaventura musician, composer of 'Mi Buenaventura' (biographical sources, El País Cali).

roleplay.goal: Persuade the group director not to accuse the rival group or withdraw, and explain what is really wrong with the marimba.
roleplay.register: usted, respectful but firm

c1-03.scene: Night courtyard of a modest Cali hostel strung with festival lights: a marimba on trestles, Nayibe with a laptop and clip-on tuner, Celestino in a white shirt shaving a key with a small knife, guadua tubes on the floor. Warm wood browns, guadua green, festival yellow and purple.

c1-04.title: Chupe en tiempo de veda
c1-04.setting: Arequipa (picanterías of Yanahuara and Cayma) and the Majes valley, Peru; a Friday in March (Lent and the river-shrimp closed season), present day.
c1-04.logline: Teófilo Zegarra, 40, runs his late grandmother's picantería in Arequipa and has one Friday in March to win back a Lima critic who once panned him. The river-shrimp season is closed until 31 March, yet the whole city says his rival doña Nieves Postigo is serving chupe de camarones, and his own supplier, el Chato Valdivia, offers him a dripping sack, no questions asked. Teófilo refuses and cooks a Lenten chupe without shrimp; at Nieves's table he discovers she never served shrimp at all, and that the rumour was the Chato's way of selling poached shrimp.

topics.topic: Concessives beyond aunque: si bien, aun cuando, por más que
topics.notes: si bien (+ indicative, formal), aun cuando and a pesar de que (indicative = fact; subjunctive = possibility or conceded point), por más que (+ subjunctive or indicative). Temptation and principle. «Aun cuando el chupe sea el plato del viernes, en marzo no se pesca camarón.» «A pesar de que el Chato juraba que era legal, el costal olía a río recién pescado.»

topics.topic: Cause and consequence: de ahí que, no porque… sino porque
topics.notes: de ahí que + subjunctive (the consequence is presented as known) and the rejected cause no porque + subjunctive… sino porque + indicative. How the rumour spread and why Teófilo goes. «El rumor corrió por todo Yanahuara; de ahí que medio Arequipa hiciera cola donde doña Nieves.» «No fui porque tuviera hambre, sino porque necesitaba ver ese chupe.»

topics.topic: Idiomatic ser and estar: estar de, estar por, ser de lo más
topics.notes: ser/estar/ir in fixed patterns: estar de + role (estuvo de cocinera), estar por + infinitive, ser de lo más + adjective, ir en serio, ir con alguien. Character and situation. «Mi abuela era de lo más exigente con el rocoto.» «Estoy por cerrar y abrir una pollería.» «El crítico está de paso hasta el sábado.» «Esto va en serio, Chato.»

topics.topic: Register shifts: tú, usted and vos
topics.notes: The same speaker moving between usted, tú and regional vos (Honduran, Arequipeño) according to role, emotion and audience, with the matching verb forms. Arequipeño voseo with friends, usted with customers. «¿Vos sabís lo que pasa si te chapan, Chato?» «¿El señor desea probar el chupe de la casa?»

c1-04.register: Colloquial kitchen talk, polite service register, the critic's printed review (formal, slightly pompous) quoted at the start and end.
c1-04.dialect: Arequipeño Spanish: traditional voseo with -ís forms (vos sabís, vos tenís) among old friends, usted for customers; local words: picantería, chicha de guiñapo, batán, lonccos (rural Arequipeños). Flag forms for review by an Arequipa speaker.
idioms: Pan para hoy, hambre para mañana: a short-term fix that causes long-term harm
hacerse el loco: to pretend not to notice
a falta de pan, buenas son tortas: make do with what you have
meter la pata: to put your foot in it
c1-04.vocabFocus: Arequipa cuisine and regulation: la picantería, el chupe, el camarón de río, la veda, el rocoto relleno, la ocopa, la chicha de guiñapo, el batán, el fogón de leña, el costal, el decomiso, el inspector, la multa, la Cuaresma, el comensal, la reseña, la sazón, las habas
facts: The picantería arequipeña was declared Patrimonio Cultural de la Nación by Resolución Viceministerial 033-2014-VMPCIC-MC, 16 April 2014 (Ministerio de Cultura del Perú).
River-shrimp extraction and sale are banned in a closed season (veda) from early January (2 or 3 Jan) to 31 March; exact dates vary by year (PRODUCE / Gobierno Regional de Arequipa notices).
Chupe de camarones is a traditional Arequipa dish, customarily served on Fridays (Arequipa gastronomy sources; Andina).
Traditional Arequipeño speech preserves voseo (Peruvian dialectology; verify the exact verb forms with a local speaker).

roleplay.goal: Turn down the illegal shrimp politely but firmly, and find out who started the rumour about doña Nieves.
roleplay.register: colloquial Arequipeño vos/tú between old acquaintances

c1-04.scene: Courtyard of a picantería with white sillar walls and the Misti volcano behind: Teófilo at a wood fire with a large clay pot, a dripping burlap sack on the floor, a grinding stone (batán), the critic with a notebook at a long table. White sillar, rocoto red, terracotta, deep blue sky.

C1-W4: I can write a persuasive letter or message that adapts its tone to the reader and sets out conditions and concessions.

c1-05.title: La voz de Triunfo
c1-05.setting: Triunfo de la Cruz, near Tela (Atlántida), Honduras; the first two weeks of April, before the 12 April commemoration of the Garífuna arrival, present day.
c1-05.logline: Dionisio Arzú, 41, producer at a small Garífuna community radio station, is preparing the 12 April special when a hotel developer offers to pay for a new transmitter on one condition: the broadcast must not mention the 2015 Inter-American Court ruling on the community's land. At the same time an unlabelled reel turns up in the storeroom: a woman singing in Garifuna whom no one can identify. With 17-year-old intern Keyla Suazo, Dionisio traces the voice to his own great-aunt Paulina Guity, whose song is about the land itself; he turns down the sponsor, airs the song with the ruling, and the community pays for the transmitter through a radio-thon.

topics.topic: Conditional conjunctions: siempre y cuando, a no ser que, con tal de que
topics.notes: Conjunctions that always take the subjunctive and set precise conditions or exceptions (siempre y cuando, con tal de que, a no ser que, en caso de que), in negotiation or legal wording. The sponsorship negotiation and the station's own rules. «Les pagamos el transmisor, siempre y cuando el especial no mencione la sentencia.» «No sale al aire a no ser que alguien identifique la voz.» «Con tal de que la gente escuche a doña Paulina, me da igual el patrocinio.»

topics.topic: Formal connectors: no obstante, a raíz de, por consiguiente
topics.notes: Written-register connectors beyond B2's sin embargo/en cambio: no obstante, a raíz de, por consiguiente, en virtud de, dicho esto. Dionisio's on-air script and the station's letter. «No obstante, una emisora comunitaria no puede depender de un solo patrocinador.» «A raíz de la sentencia de 2015, el Estado debía titular las tierras.» «Por consiguiente, el especial durará tres horas.»

topics.topic: Reporting verbs: negar haber, alegar, admitir
topics.notes: Precise reporting verbs with their constructions: negar/admitir + compound infinitive, alegar/asegurar que + indicative, advertir de que, exigir que + subjunctive. Reporting the sponsor's claims and the elders' testimony on air. «La licenciada Zelaya aseguró que la empresa respetaba a la comunidad.» «El abuelo de Keyla admitió haber grabado la cinta en los años ochenta.»

topics.topic: Register shifts: tú, usted and vos
topics.notes: The same speaker moving between usted, tú and regional vos (Honduran, Arequipeño) according to role, emotion and audience, with the matching verb forms. Honduran voseo with Keyla, usted with the sponsor, radio-presenter ustedes. «Vos sabés que no podemos, Keyla.» «Usted comprenderá, licenciada, que eso no es negociable.»

c1-05.register: Radio presenting (warm, formal-public), negotiation in formal usted, colloquial Honduran voseo in the booth; short Garifuna greetings.
c1-05.dialect: Honduran Spanish with voseo (vos sabés, andá), cipota (girl), maje (mate), pisto (money); Garifuna words glossed (buiti binafi 'good morning', seremein 'thank you', hudutu, garaon drums). Garifuna items to be checked by a Garifuna speaker.
idioms: Lo barato sale caro: cheap things end up costing more
tener la sartén por el mango: to have the upper hand
más vale solo que mal acompañado: better alone than in bad company
no dar el brazo a torcer: to stand firm
c1-05.vocabFocus: Community radio and land rights: la emisora comunitaria, el transmisor, la frecuencia, la cabina, la consola, la cinta, el carrete, la locución, el patrocinio, la cuña, la parrilla de programación, la sentencia, el título colectivo, el territorio ancestral, el tambor garaon, la punta, el hudutu
facts: The Garífuna arrived in Honduras (Roatán) on 12 April 1797 after being deported by the British from St Vincent; 12 April is commemorated in Honduras (historiography; Honduran commemorations).
The language, dance and music of the Garifuna were proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001 (Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua; UNESCO).

Inter-American Court of Human Rights, Comunidad Garífuna Triunfo de la Cruz y sus miembros vs. Honduras, judgment of 8 October 2015 (Serie C No. 305): violation of collective property; ordered demarcation and collective title (Corte IDH).
Hudutu (plantain mash with fish in coconut broth) and garaon drums are Garífuna traditions (ethnographic sources).

roleplay.goal: Negotiate the sponsorship: state your conditions clearly and refuse censorship without closing the door.
roleplay.register: formal usted, negotiation

c1-05.scene: A wooden radio booth on stilts near a Caribbean beach with coconut palms: Dionisio in headphones at an old console, Keyla holding a reel-to-reel tape up to the light, a garaon drum in the corner, a hand-painted station sign. Turquoise, white sand, red and yellow logo, wood brown.

C1-R2: I can recognise shifts of register in a text, from an official report or legal clause to casual dialogue, and explain why the writer uses each one.

c1-06.title: La casa que cruzó el canal
c1-06.titleEn: The House That Crossed the Channel
c1-06.setting: Castro and Quinchao island, Chiloé archipelago, Chile; late February, present day.
c1-06.logline: Javiera Oyarzún, 36, a municipal planner in Castro, must approve or block a minga to tow an old shingled house by sea from Quinchao to Chiloé, and its owner, Belarmino Cárcamo, 81, demands one particular Sunday and no other. The forecast is bad, the insurance rules are worse, and his grandson Yerko suspects the old man only wants to move the house to sell it. Javiera discovers that the date matches the year's highest tide, the only one that lets the house float over the reef to the plot where his late wife was born; she approves the minga with conditions, one tide later, and the whole island pulls.

topics.topic: Conditions without si: de + infinitive, de no ser por
topics.notes: Compact counterfactuals: de + (compound) infinitive and de no ser por + noun replacing si-clauses, with the conditional perfect in the main clause. Risk talk between planner, harbour office and owner. «De no ser por la marea, la casa encallaría frente a Achao.» «De haberlo sabido antes, habría pedido el informe de la Armada.»

topics.topic: Formal connectors: no obstante, a raíz de, por consiguiente
topics.notes: Written-register connectors beyond B2's sin embargo/en cambio: no obstante, a raíz de, por consiguiente, en virtud de, dicho esto. Javiera's municipal resolution. «A raíz del temporal, la Capitanía de Puerto suspendió la navegación.» «Por consiguiente, la minga queda autorizada para el domingo siguiente.»

topics.topic: Periphrases: llegar a, terminar por, dar por + participle
topics.notes: llegar a + infinitive (culmination, even…), terminar/acabar por + infinitive (end up), dar por + participle (take as given: dar por hecho, dar por perdido). Stubbornness and its outcome. «Don Belarmino llegó a amenazar con remolcarla él solo.» «Yerko dio por hecho que su abuelo quería vender.» «El viejo terminó por aceptar.»

topics.topic: Hedging and intensifying: al parecer, más bien, de lo más
topics.notes: Attenuation (al parecer, digamos, más bien, no es que + subjunctive, cabe suponer) and intensification (de lo más, sumamente, ni siquiera) to manage politeness and commitment. Diplomacy with an elder and with the council. «Al parecer, la casa tiene más de cien años.» «No es que me oponga, don Belarmino; más bien me preocupa el viento.»

c1-06.register: Municipal resolution and council emails (formal, nominal), polite usted with the elder, colloquial Chilean between Javiera and Yerko.

Tides in the inner sea of Chiloé have a range of several metres (SHOA tide tables) – keep figures general.

c1-06.scene: A two-storey wooden house with yellow and red shingles floating on barrels in a grey-green channel, pulled by small fishing boats; on shore a crowd, a pair of oxen and Javiera in a hard hat with a tablet, the old man standing on the porch of the floating house. c1-07.title: La pregunta que faltaba
c1-07.setting: Cuajinicuilapa, Costa Chica de Guerrero, Mexico; March 2020, the last days of census fieldwork.
c1-07.logline: Itandehui Cruz, 26, a census enumerator from Oaxaca city, must close her last blocks in Cuajinicuilapa before the 27 March deadline, and one household will not let her finish the questionnaire. Doña Eufemia Noyola, 93, says nobody in her house will answer the new question on Afro-Mexican self-identification, while her grandson Baltazar, 35, a teacher who campaigned for that question, insists they will. Over three visits, a Danza de los Diablos mask and an afternoon at the Museo de las Culturas Afromestizas, Itandehui learns why the word 'negra' once hurt, and doña Eufemia answers for herself, in her own words.

topics.topic: Present perfect subjunctive: haya + participle
topics.notes: First headline for haya + participle (absent at B1/B2): past or completed events seen from a present that requires the subjunctive (no creo que, me alegra que, cuando + future completion). Feelings and doubts about what has happened. «Me alegra que hayas vuelto, muchacha.» «No es posible que hayan contado mal en 2015.» «Cuando hayan contestado todos, cierro el cuestionario.»

topics.topic: Venir and andar + gerund
topics.notes: venir + gerund for a process continuing up to now (vienen preguntando desde 2015) and andar + gerund for a repeated, often disapproved activity (anda diciendo). Long processes and gossip. «Los del gobierno vienen preguntando lo mismo desde hace años.» «Mi nieto anda diciendo que somos afromexicanos, como si yo no lo supiera.»

topics.topic: Hedging and intensifying: al parecer, más bien, de lo más
topics.notes: Attenuation (al parecer, digamos, más bien, no es que + subjunctive, cabe suponer) and intensification (de lo más, sumamente, ni siquiera) to manage politeness and commitment. Itandehui's careful questions and the elder's evasions. «Digamos que en mis tiempos esa palabra no se decía bonito.» «No es que no quiera contestar; es que la pregunta llega tarde.»

c1-07.register: Questionnaire usted (scripted, formal), tactful improvised usted, Baltazar's activist register, the grandmother's colloquial storytelling.
c1-07.dialect: Costa Chica Mexican Spanish: ahorita, mero, ¿mande?, pues; local words redondo (traditional round house), chilena (local music genre), Danza de los Diablos.
idioms: Más sabe el diablo por viejo que por diablo: experience beats cleverness

Al pan, pan, y al vino, vino: call a spade a spade

C1-R4: I can understand idioms, sayings and cultural references in context, including terms from Afro-Latin traditions (marimba de chonta, Garífuna, liberto, Danza de los Diablos).

c1-08.title: El real que no sonaba
c1-08.setting: Casa Nacional de Moneda, Potosí, Bolivia; present day, with the mint scandal of the 1640s as background.
c1-08.logline: Ofelia Choque, 52, a conservator at the Casa Nacional de Moneda in Potosí, is asked to authenticate a hand-struck eight-real coin (a macuquina) that the collector Gastón Aramayo wants to sell abroad as a 1649 rarity. The coin weighs right but rings wrong, and her young assistant Wara is sure it is a modern fake. Ofelia proves it is genuine: a debased coin from the Potosí mint fraud of the 1640s, worthless as silver and priceless as evidence, and as national heritage it cannot leave the country.

topics.topic: Pluperfect subjunctive in subordinate clauses
topics.notes: hubiera + participle after a past main verb in purpose, temporal, concessive and evaluative clauses (sin que, antes de que, era improbable que), not in si-clauses (those were B2). Seventeenth-century fraud seen from the past. «Era improbable que alguien la hubiera falsificado con plata de esa ley.» «Se acuñaron miles de piezas sin que nadie hubiera comprobado su ley.»

topics.topic: Impersonal se with people vs pasiva refleja
topics.notes: Choosing between pasiva refleja with things (se cargaron dos neveras), impersonal se + a with people (se citó a los estibadores, no se sancionará a nadie) and ser + participle for official acts. History-book and lab-report style. «La moneda fue acuñada en Potosí hacia 1649.» «Se fundieron las piezas defectuosas.» «Se condenó a varios responsables.»

topics.topic: Future perfect: completion and conjecture
topics.notes: habrá + participle for completion before a future point (para el viernes habrá secado) and for guesses about the past (¿quién habrá abierto la caja?); B2 had only the conditional perfect. Waiting for results and imagining the coin's journey. «Para mañana ya habrá llegado el análisis del laboratorio.» «¿Por cuántas manos habrá pasado esta moneda?»

topics.topic: Periphrases: llegar a, terminar por, dar por + participle
topics.notes: llegar a + infinitive (culmination, even…), terminar/acabar por + infinitive (end up), dar por + participle (take as given: dar por hecho, dar por perdido). Scale and assumptions. «El escándalo llegó a preocupar al mismísimo rey.» «Wara dio por sentado que era falsa.»

c1-08.register: Technical conservation report and museum labels (formal, passive), negotiation with the collector (formal usted), colleague banter (tú).
c1-08.dialect: Bolivian Andean Spanish: nomás, pues, ¿ya?, frequent diminutives; Aymara/Quechua words in context (Wara 'star', jallalla 'cheers/long live').
idioms: Vale un Potosí: it's worth a fortune (from Don Quijote)
No es oro todo lo que reluce: all that glitters is not gold
pagar con la misma moneda: to pay someone back in kind
ser moneda corriente: to be commonplace
c1-08.vocabFocus: Coinage and heritage: la ceca, la acuñación, la macuquina, el real de a ocho, la ley (fineness), la aleación, el ensayador, la balanza de precisión, el cuño, el anverso, la falsificación, el visitador, el patrimonio, la exportación, fundir, el sello, el lingote
facts: The City of Potosí was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 (UNESCO WHC).
The present Casa Nacional de Moneda building dates from the 18th century (built c. 1753–1773) and is now a museum (Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia).
Macuquinas are irregular hand-struck 'cob' coins (numismatic reference).

In the 1640s the Potosí mint issued debased silver coins; the scandal was investigated by visitador Francisco de Nestares Marín and led to punishments and a redesign of the coinage in the early 1650s (numismatic and colonial-history literature; verify dates before writing).
Bolivian heritage law restricts the export of cultural property (Ley 530 de Patrimonio Cultural Boliviano, 2014; verify the article used).

roleplay.goal: Explain why the coin cannot leave the country and propose an alternative (loan or sale to the museum).
roleplay.register: formal usted, firm and diplomatic

c1-08.scene: Conservation lab in a stone colonial building with arches: Ofelia with a loupe and white gloves over a crude silver coin on black velvet, a precision scale, Wara at a laptop, Cerro Rico through the window. Silver, stone grey, deep red, cobalt sky.

C1-R1: I can follow a long story with several timelines and embedded documents (reports, ledgers, wills, scripts) and say what is established and what is only inferred.

c1-09.title: El cocinero de la goleta
c1-09.setting: An archive reading room in San Juan, Puerto Rico (present day), and the ports of San Juan, Santo Domingo and Havana, 1872–1876.
c1-09.logline: Ezequiel Rivera Ortiz, 47, an archivist in San Juan, receives a request from Altagracia Peguero, 38, a Dominican lawyer tracing an ancestor named Tiburcio who appears in Puerto Rico's 1872 slave register. Tiburcio vanishes from the records after abolition in 1873, then reappears as cook on a schooner bound for Havana, where slavery was still legal, which makes no sense to either of them. Through crew lists and port ledgers Ezequiel finds that Tiburcio's three-year post-abolition contract was with the schooner's captain, and that he left the ship in Santo Domingo, where he could not be re-enslaved, the day before it sailed for Havana.

topics.topic: Pluperfect subjunctive in subordinate clauses
topics.notes: hubiera + participle after a past main verb in purpose, temporal, concessive and evaluative clauses (sin que, antes de que, era improbable que), not in si-clauses (those were B2). Reasoning about what had happened. «Le parecía improbable que un liberto se hubiera embarcado hacia La Habana por voluntad propia.» «Desembarcó sin que el capitán lo hubiera anotado en el rol.»

topics.topic: Formal relatives: el cual, lo cual
topics.notes: el cual / la cual after longer or compound prepositions (desde el cual, a raíz de la cual) and lo cual referring back to a whole clause; B2 already covered en el que and cuyo. Archival prose. «El registro de 1872, en el cual figuraba Tiburcio, ocupa tres estanterías.» «La goleta zarpó un martes, lo cual coincide con la fecha del contrato.»

topics.topic: Nominalization in formal register
topics.notes: Turning verbs into nouns to pack information in reports, archive notes and legal texts (la llegada, la apertura, la consulta, la puesta en marcha), with the matching light verbs (tener lugar, llevar a cabo, dar inicio). Ezequiel's research note and the archive's rules. «La abolición no supuso la libertad inmediata, sino la firma de contratos obligatorios.» «La consulta del rol de tripulantes requiere autorización previa.»

topics.topic: Compound infinitive and gerund: tras haber, habiendo
topics.notes: haber + participle in non-finite forms to mark anteriority in formal narration: tras haber, por no haber, habiendo + participle. Formal narration of sequence. «Tras haber cumplido dieciocho meses de contrato, Tiburcio desaparece de los libros.» «Habiendo revisado los tres libros, Ezequiel llamó a Santo Domingo.»

c1-09.register: Archival and academic formal prose, 19th-century ledger entries (quoted, with abbreviations), video-call dialogue moving from usted to tú.
c1-09.dialect: Puerto Rican Spanish (tú, ustedes; bregar, chavos) and Dominican Spanish (vaina, un chin, ¿Qué tal, licenciado?); 19th-century documentary Spanish in quotations (D., dho., vecino de esta plaza).
idioms: buscar una aguja en un pajar: to look for a needle in a haystack
atar cabos: to put two and two together
El que busca, encuentra: seek and you shall find
Poco a poco se llega lejos: slowly but surely
c1-09.vocabFocus: Archives and maritime records: el legajo, el rol de tripulantes, el libro de entradas y salidas, la goleta, el bergantín, el liberto, el contrato de trabajo, la cédula, el registro, el folio, el asiento, la Capitanía del Puerto, la tachadura, la consulta, el descendiente, la partida de bautismo, zarpar
facts: Slavery in Puerto Rico was abolished by the law of 22 March 1873; freed people (libertos) were obliged to sign labour contracts for three years (Puerto Rican historiography; Primera Hora 150th-anniversary coverage).
The Registro Central de Esclavos of 1872 recorded name, origin, residence, occupation, age, physical description and owner (archival catalogues).
In Cuba, slavery was converted into the 'patronato' in 1880 and ended in 1886 (Cuban historiography).
In Santo Domingo slavery was abolished in 1822 under Haitian rule (Dominican historiography).
The Archivo General de Puerto Rico (Instituto de Cultura Puertorriqueña) is in San Juan. Keep the story's archive generic unless the details are checked.

roleplay.goal: Explain your findings to the descendant by video call: what is proven, what is probable and what remains unknown.
roleplay.register: usted at first, then tú; careful hedging

c1-09.scene: Archive reading room with tall windows over San Juan bay: Ezequiel in cotton gloves turning a huge leather ledger, a laptop showing Altagracia on a video call from Santo Domingo, a pencil drawing of a schooner pinned above the desk. Parchment beige, Caribbean blue, mahogany.

C1-W1: I can write a clear, well-structured formal text, such as an incident report, an archive note or a council resolution, using nominalisation, impersonal se and formal connectors.

c1-10.title: La torta negra de la señora Pugh
c1-10.setting: Gaiman and Trelew, Chubut (Argentine Patagonia); July, the week of 28 July (Welsh landing day), present day.
c1-10.logline: Lautaro Jones, 58, a lawyer in Trelew, must execute the will of Nesta Pugh, 88, owner of Gaiman's oldest Welsh tea house: the house goes to her nephew Ceferino Toledo, but 'the recipe' goes to 'whoever made it'. Both Ceferino and Brígida Maldonado, the tea house's cook for thirty years, claim the famous torta negra, and nothing can be signed until Lautaro decides. In a recipe notebook in Welsh and Spanish he finds that since 1994 the recipe has been rewritten in Brígida's hand, so the recipe is hers, and he gets both heirs to sign an agreement to keep baking it in the same house.

topics.topic: Conditional conjunctions: siempre y cuando, a no ser que, con tal de que
topics.notes: Conjunctions that always take the subjunctive and set precise conditions or exceptions (siempre y cuando, con tal de que, a no ser que, en caso de que), in negotiation or legal wording. The will's clauses and the heirs' demands. «Lego la receta a quien la haya hecho, siempre y cuando siga horneándola en Gaiman.» «En caso de que hubiera dos pretendientes, decidirá el albacea.» «No firmo nada a no ser que me dejen ver el cuaderno.»

topics.topic: Nominalization in formal register
topics.notes: Turning verbs into nouns to pack information in reports, archive notes and legal texts (la llegada, la apertura, la consulta, la puesta en marcha), with the matching light verbs (tener lugar, llevar a cabo, dar inicio). Legal and notarial prose. «La apertura del testamento tuvo lugar el lunes.» «La redacción de la cláusula admite dos lecturas.»

topics.topic: Pseudo-clefts: lo que pasó fue que
topics.notes: lo que / lo único que / quien … + ser to put the new information at the end (lo que me molesta es…, lo que pasó fue que…); B2 covered fue X quien. Arguing about what the text actually says. «Lo que dice el testamento es “quien la hizo”, no “quien la inventó”.» «Lo que me duele es que nadie me haya preguntado.»

topics.topic: Idiomatic ser and estar: estar de, estar por, ser de lo más
topics.notes: ser/estar/ir in fixed patterns: estar de + role (estuvo de cocinera), estar por + infinitive, ser de lo más + adjective, ir en serio, ir con alguien. People and situations. «La tía Nesta era de lo más ordenada.» «Brígida estuvo de cocinera treinta años.» «Estoy por renunciar al caso.»

c1-10.register: Testamentary and notarial language (quoted clauses), Lautaro's formal letters, Rioplatense colloquial with voseo, a few Welsh words.
c1-10.dialect: Argentine Patagonian Spanish with voseo (vos sabés, mirá, che), ustedes; Welsh-Patagonian vocabulary: te galés, torta negra, capilla, Eisteddfod, bara brith.
idioms: Cada maestrito con su librito (Argentina): everyone has their own way of doing things
Cuentas claras, amistades largas: clear accounts make lasting friendships
meter la cuchara: to butt in
ser pan comido: to be a piece of cake

facts: Welsh settlers arrived at Puerto Madryn aboard the Mimosa on 28 July 1865, commemorated in Chubut as the Día del Desembarco / Gŵyl y Glaniad (Chubut provincial history).
Gaiman is known for its Welsh tea houses and the torta negra galesa (Chubut tourism and heritage sources).
The Eisteddfod del Chubut is held annually (Trelew/Gaiman cultural calendar).
In Argentina an executor (albacea) carries out a will under the Código Civil y Comercial (2015); keep the legal detail general.

roleplay.register: usted moving to vos; Rioplatense

c1-10.scene: Wood-panelled Welsh tea house in Gaiman in winter: a table set with china and a dark fruit cake, an old notebook open with Welsh and Spanish handwriting, Lautaro in a suit with reading glasses, a woman in an apron and a younger man facing each other; bare poplars outside the window. c2-01.title: Cuplé de autor
c2-01.setting: Cádiz (barrio de La Viña and the Gran Teatro Falla), Spain; January–February, during the COAC carnival contest, present day.
c2-01.logline: Reyes Garrido, 63, a retired judge who writes the lyrics for a neighbourhood chirigota, hears her best cuplé sung almost word for word by a rival group in the preliminaries, three days before her own group performs. Everyone blames Fali Camacho, the rival author with an old grudge, and Reyes investigates with the habits of her old courtroom: rehearsal recordings, message timestamps and a rhyme that does not quite fit. The evidence convicts no one but herself: both cuplés echo a forgotten 1980s chirigota by an author they both admired, which she had half-remembered as her own, so she rewrites the cuplé overnight as a joke about herself and wins the theatre.

topics.topic: Irony, understatement and litotes
topics.notes: Saying less than one means (no está nada mal, poco original), ironic praise, and their signals (digamos, con modestia ejemplar). The narrator's dry judge's voice. «No es que el cuplé fuera malo: era, digamos, poco original.» «Una jueza que se condena a sí misma: no está nada mal para un martes.»

topics.topic: Proverbs and truncated refranes
topics.notes: Proverbs quoted whole, cut short for the listener to complete (quien roba a un ladrón…) or twisted for irony. Proverbs the chirigota lives on, often left unfinished. «En casa del herrero, cuchillo de palo.» «Cría fama y échate a dormir.» «Quien roba a un ladrón…»

topics.topic: Mood for stance: aunque, el hecho de que, como
topics.notes: Subjunctive for known facts treated as irrelevant (aunque sea un sinvergüenza), el hecho de que + subjunctive or indicative, como + subjunctive as a threat/condition vs como + indicative as cause. Judging facts versus judging people. «Aunque Fali sea un sinvergüenza, esta vez no ha robado nada.» «El hecho de que la rima coincida no prueba nada.» «Como no aparezca la grabación, no hay caso.»

topics.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
topics.notes: Fixed subjunctive formulas in speech: ¡ni que fuera…!, que yo sepa, como quien no quiere la cosa, que digamos, sea como sea. Rehearsal-room banter. «¡Ni que fuera la primera vez que alguien canta un chiste viejo!» «Que yo sepa, nadie grabó el ensayo.» «Como quien no quiere la cosa, Fali se sentó en la última fila.»

c2-01.register: Ironic first-person narration with judicial vocabulary, Andalusian colloquial dialogue, sung carnival verses (cuplé and estribillo) quoted in full.
c2-01.dialect: Western Andalusian (Cádiz): seseo/ceceo and s-aspiration (suggested in the audio, not in the spelling), ustedes with vosotros verb forms in informal speech (ustedes os vais), quillo/illo, mi arma, jartible.
idioms: En casa del herrero, cuchillo de palo: the cobbler's children go barefoot
Cría fama y échate a dormir: once you have a reputation it sticks
Piensa mal y acertarás: think the worst and you'll be right
Nada nuevo bajo el sol: nothing new under the sun
c2-01.vocabFocus: Carnival and evidence: la chirigota, la comparsa, el cuplé, el pasodoble, el estribillo, la letra, el letrista, el tipo (costume), las preliminares, el concurso, el ensayo, la peña, la rima, el plagio, la grabación, la prueba, el veredicto, el bombo y la caja, el pito de carnaval
facts: The COAC (Concurso Oficial de Agrupaciones Carnavalescas) of Cádiz is held at the Gran Teatro Falla, with four categories: comparsas, chirigotas, coros and cuartetos (Ayuntamiento de Cádiz).
A chirigota's repertoire includes a presentación, pasodobles, cuplés with an estribillo and a popurrí (contest rules).
Western Andalusian ustedes combined with second-person-plural verb forms is a documented dialect feature (RAE/ASALE Nueva gramática; Andalusian dialectology).

roleplay.goal: Raise the matter of the identical cuplé with the rival author using irony, without accusing him outright.
roleplay.register: colloquial Andalusian tú

c2-01.scene: Backstage at a red-and-gold theatre: chirigoteros dressed as judges in wigs and gowns in front of bulb-lit mirrors, Reyes in reading glasses holding a phone with a sound wave on screen and a notebook, kazoos and a bass drum on a chair. Theatre red and gold, black-and-white costumes, confetti.
canDo: C2-S1: I can argue a case before a demanding audience, anticipating objections and using rhetorical devices effectively.
C2-R3: I can recognise irony, understatement, litotes and rhetorical devices, and explain the implicit meaning and the writer's attitude.

c2-02.title: La lonja del Mediomundo
c2-02.setting: Montevideo (Barrio Sur and Palermo), Uruguay; late January to the Desfile de Llamadas in February, present day, with memories of the 1978 eviction.
c2-02.logline: Obdulio Pereyra, 72, a retired typographer who has played the piano drum in his comparsa's line for fifty years, finds a crack in the old drum he inherited from his father, made in the Mediomundo tenement before its demolition, days before the Llamadas. His daughter Mirtha, 45, a nurse, wants him to retire, and drum-maker el Cholo Larrosa will only repair it if Obdulio lets him see what is under the lining. Told largely through Obdulio's thoughts, the story reveals that his father wrote inside the drum the names of the families evicted from Mediomundo; the drum is rebuilt with the names intact, and Obdulio walks the Llamadas beside his granddaughter Abigail, who plays it.

topics.topic: Free indirect speech
topics.notes: A character's thoughts rendered in third-person past narration without verbs of saying: questions, exclamations, deictics (mañana, aquí) and the character's own vocabulary inside the narrator's voice. Obdulio's thoughts inside the narration. «¿Retirarse? ¿Él? Cincuenta años en la cuerda y ahora venía la nena a decirle lo que tenía que hacer.» «Mañana, sí, mañana lo llevaría al taller; hoy no.»

topics.topic: Ellipsis and fragments in narration
topics.notes: Verbless sentences, nominal fragments and gapped verbs for rhythm, tension or note-taking style; the reader recovers the missing verb from context. Rhythm of memory and drumming. «Cuero nuevo, aro nuevo. El sonido, el de siempre.» «¿El tambor? En el ropero. ¿La lonja? Rajada.»

topics.topic: Left dislocation and clitic doubling
topics.notes: Topic first, pronoun after (A mi viejo lo sacaron…; Eso ya lo sabíamos), Rioplatense doubling of full direct objects (lo conocí a tu abuelo) and Andean invariable lo (esa carretera lo están ensanchando). c2-03.title: Las letras rusas de la etiqueta
c2-03.titleEn: The Russian Letters on the Label
c2-03.setting: Valle de Guadalupe and Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico; August (Fiestas de la Vendimia), present day.
c2-03.logline: Leobardo Rogel, 39, a winemaker in the Valle de Guadalupe, is asked to sit on a blind-tasting panel before a charity auction where a bottle with a handwritten Cyrillic label, presented as 1930s wine from the valley's Molokan settlers, is expected to fetch a fortune. The bottle's owner, a polished Mexico City sommelier named Iker Alcocer, has a perfect story; Leobardo's palate and a conversation with Nikolái Bogdánov, 86, a Molokan descendant, say otherwise. The wine is genuine Molokan home wine, but from 1979, made by Nikolái's mother from the family's last row of vines on a recycled old label; the auction turns into a tribute, and the wine turns out to be better than its legend.

topics.topic: Concessive and conjectural future and conditional
topics.notes: Future/conditional of conjecture woven into narration and their concessive use (será muy famoso, pero…; tendría razón, pero…), beyond B2's single-sentence conjecture. Doubts in narration and concessive guesses. «Será muy de la capital, pero de vino sabe.» «Tendría razón el catálogo, pero ese corcho no tenía noventa años.» «¿Quién habrá escrito esas letras?»

topics.topic: Por poco, por poco que
topics.notes: por poco + present indicative for a near miss in the past (por poco se me cae), por poco que + subjunctive (however little), con lo que + indicative (considering how much). Near misses and minimal knowledge. «Por poco se me cae la copa.» «Por poco que supiera de vinos, cualquiera notaría esa acidez.» «Con lo que me costó llegar hasta aquí, no pienso callarme.»

topics.topic: Irony, understatement and litotes
topics.notes: Saying less than one means (no está nada mal, poco original), ironic praise, and their signals (digamos, con modestia ejemplar). The auction catalogue and its reader. «El vino, explicó Iker con modestia ejemplar, era sencillamente un milagro.» «No era mal vino. Era, sencillamente, otro vino.»

topics.topic: Colloquial subjunctive formulas: ni que fuera, que yo sepa
topics.notes: Fixed subjunctive formulas in speech: ¡ni que fuera…!, que yo sepa, como quien no quiere la cosa, que digamos, sea como sea. Northern Mexican banter. «¡Ni que fuera vino de misa!» «Que yo sepa, los molokanes no vendían vino.» «Como quien no quiere la cosa, Nikolái sacó una foto.»

c2-03.register: Technical tasting notes, a pompous auction catalogue (ironized), relaxed northern Mexican dialogue, Nikolái's older formal Spanish.
c2-03.dialect: Northern Mexican / Baja California Spanish: ¿qué onda?, ahorita, morro (kid), troca (truck), raite (ride); a few Russian words of the Molokan community in context.
idioms: dar gato por liebre: to pass off something inferior as the real thing

facts: Molokans (Russian 'spiritual Christians' from the Kars region) settled the Valle de Guadalupe around 1905–1906 (Molokan community histories; Museo Bibayoff; sources differ on the year).
The Molokans made wine mainly for their own use and planted vineyards around 1915; mission-era vines and Bodegas Santo Tomás (founded 1888) came earlier (regional wine histories).
The Fiestas de la Vendimia take place in the valley every August (Provino Baja California).
After the 1930s agrarian reform the settlement became the ejido Francisco Zarco (local history; verify).

roleplay.goal: Tell the sommelier, tactfully but firmly, that his story about the bottle does not hold, and suggest an honest way to present it.
roleplay.register: tú between professionals, with polite irony

Golden orange, wine purple, sage hills.

c2-04.title: La copla de Tocaña
c2-04.setting: Tocaña and Coroico (Nor Yungas, La Paz department), Bolivia; rainy season, present day.
c2-04.logline: Simona Angola, 29, an Afro-Bolivian civil engineer who grew up in Tocaña and now works for the departmental roads service, comes home to supervise the widening of the road, and finds a new saya copla going round that mocks the project and, without naming her, mocks her. Everyone knows the coplas are sung by the elder Jacinta Barra, 77, but Jacinta says she did not write this one. Tracing a technical word in the verse that only an insider would know, Simona finds that Jacinta did write it, with help from the site's own drainage foreman, and that the copla warns, correctly, that the planned drain will flood the old cemetery; Simona redesigns the drainage, and the next copla praises her, with a sting in the tail.

topics.topic: Left dislocation and clitic doubling
topics.notes: Topic first, pronoun after (A mi viejo lo sacaron…; Eso ya lo sabíamos), Rioplatense doubling of full direct objects (lo conocí a tu abuelo) and Andean invariable lo (esa carretera lo están ensanchando). Andean topic-first syntax and clitics (used by older speakers, never as caricature). «A la Jacinta yo no la vi cantar esa copla.» «Esa carretera ya lo están ensanchando, dice.»

topics.topic: Diminutives and augmentatives: pragmatics
topics.notes: -ito/-ita, Andean -ito for politeness, Asturian -ín/-ina, -ón/-ota and -ucho for affection, irony, softening or contempt; the suffix as stance, not size. Politeness and irony through suffixes. «Un ratito nomás, hijita, ya está el cafecito.» «¡Qué obrita la del ingeniero!» «¿Y esa carreterota para quién es?»

topics.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
topics.notes: Evidential strategies: hearsay dizque/dice que, Guaraní ndaje in Paraguayan Spanish, Andean mirative pluperfect (¡había sido verdad!), según parece. Source and surprise. «¡Había sido verdad lo del cementerio!» «Dizque la copla la había escrito alguien de La Paz.» «Va a llover, dice.»

topics.topic: Rhetorical devices: anaphora, rhetorical questions, tricolon
topics.notes: Persuasive and poetic patterning in speeches and coplas: repeated openings, questions answered by the speaker, groups of three. The coplas themselves and Simona's speech to the community. «¿Para quién es el camino? ¿Para quién es el cemento? Para el que pasa corriendo, no para el que está durmiendo.» (anaphora, rhetorical questions)

c2-04.register: Sung coplas (oral poetry), engineering report and departmental memo, Andean colloquial dialogue.
c2-04.dialect: Bolivian Yungas Spanish with Andean features (nomás, pues, dice reportative, había sido mirative, pervasive diminutives, clitic doubling); Aymara loans (aguayo, chuspa). Afro-Yungueño speech features used lightly and only after review by community speakers.

facts: Bolivia's 2009 Constitution recognises the Afro-Bolivian people (Constitución Política del Estado, arts. 3 and 32).

The saya afroboliviana is the music and dance of Afro-Bolivian communities in the Yungas, with sung coplas and drums; the caporal dance draws on its figure of the overseer (ethnomusicology; verify the heritage law number before citing one).
Tocaña, Chicaloma and Mururata are Afro-Bolivian communities in the Yungas (ethnographic sources).
The old North Yungas road ('Camino de la Muerte') was largely replaced for traffic by a new road in the late 2000s (Bolivian roads authority; verify year).

c2-05.title: Demasiado perfecta
c2-05.setting: Joya de Cerén archaeological site and San Salvador, El Salvador; rainy season, present day.
c2-05.logline: Neftalí Chicas, 64, custodian at Joya de Cerén for thirty years, sees an online post offering an intact Classic-period pot 'from Cerén' to foreign collectors, and the next morning a national paper reports that the site has probably been looted, on his watch. His former student, archaeologist Yesenia Alas, writes the official report while the press speculates; Neftalí, who knows every hollow of the site, suspects the pot never came out of the ash. Field memory and academic method together show it is a replica made for the site's own education programme and stolen from a storeroom; the report corrects the press, and the paper corrects itself, on page 14.

topics.topic: Ellipsis and fragments in narration
topics.notes: Verbless sentences, nominal fragments and gapped verbs for rhythm, tension or note-taking style; the reader recovers the missing verb from context. Neftalí's clipped, observational narration. «¿Saqueo? ¿En Cerén? Treinta años, cada mañana, el mismo sendero.» «La olla, perfecta. Demasiado perfecta.»

topics.topic: Quizá, tal vez, a lo mejor: mood and certainty
topics.notes: quizá/tal vez + subjunctive (less likely) vs + indicative (more likely), a lo mejor and igual (always indicative), ojalá + present vs imperfect subjunctive for degrees of hope. Weighing hypotheses. «Quizá la hayan sacado de otro sitio.» versus «Quizá tiene razón el periódico.» «A lo mejor es una réplica.» «Ojalá sea falsa.»

topics.topic: Journalistic conditional: habría + participle
topics.notes: The conditional of rumour in news reports to signal unconfirmed information (la pieza habría sido extraída, según fuentes…) and how a careful writer retracts it. The news reports. «Según fuentes del ministerio, la pieza habría sido extraída del sitio durante la noche.» «El custodio habría permitido el acceso.»

topics.topic: Academic register: impersonal hedging
topics.notes: Impersonal, hedged academic prose (cabe señalar, se constata, los datos apuntan a, cabe la posibilidad de que + subjunctive) contrasted with the characters' speech. Yesenia's report. «Cabe señalar que no se constatan alteraciones en la estratigrafía.» «Los datos disponibles apuntan a una manufactura reciente.»

c2-05.register: News articles and a correction notice, an archaeological report, Salvadoran colloquial with voseo.
c2-05.dialect: Salvadoran Spanish: voseo (vos sabés, vení), cipote (kid), chivo (cool), bicho, pupusa; usted with superiors.
idioms: Ver para creer: seeing is believing
Cada quien jala agua para su molino: everyone looks after their own interests
De lo que veas, cree la mitad: believe half of what you see
Hablar más que un perico: to talk too much
c2-05.vocabFocus: Archaeology and the press: el yacimiento, la estratigrafía, la ceniza volcánica, la tefra, la erupción, el saqueo, la réplica, la cerámica policromada, la pieza, la custodia, la ficha de inventario, el peritaje, la denuncia, el titular, la fe de erratas, el comunicado, la milpa
facts: Joya de Cerén, a farming village buried by the Loma Caldera eruption around AD 600, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 and is often called the 'Pompeii of the Americas' (UNESCO WHC).
The site was found by accident in 1976 during earthworks; systematic excavation began in 1978 under Payson Sheets (site histories).
Excavations have documented household objects, buildings and cultivated fields (maize, manioc) preserved under volcanic ash (archaeological publications).

roleplay.goal: Interview the custodian as a journalist, separating what he knows from what he suspects.
roleplay.register: usted, journalistic; he slips into vos

c2-05.scene: Cerén site under protective metal roofs, adobe structures and layered ash in the trench walls; an older man in a khaki uniform holding a phone with a photo of a pot, a young woman archaeologist with a tablet and trowel. Ash grey, earth ochre, tin roofs, young maize.

c2-06.title: Lo que dijo Miss Ivy
c2-06.setting: Puerto Limón, Costa Rica; from 31 August (Día de la Persona Negra y la Cultura Afrocostarricense) to the October carnival, present day.
c2-06.logline: Leonard 'Lenny' Gayle, 52, a Limón-born journalist at a San José newspaper, publishes a story, from a single source, saying this year's Carnaval de Limón would be cancelled; it goes viral and his own city turns against him. His source turns out to have misheard Miss Ivy Campbell, 90, a retired teacher and calypso singer whose words, half in Limonese Creole, meant something quite different. To set it right Lenny has to listen to his city again: he re-interviews Miss Ivy, writes a correction that separates fact from rumour, and ends up on the parade route.

topics.topic: Journalistic conditional: habría + participle
topics.notes: The conditional of rumour in news reports to signal unconfirmed information (la pieza habría sido extraída, según fuentes…) and how a careful writer retracts it. The viral article and its retraction. «El Carnaval de Limón se habría suspendido por falta de presupuesto, según una fuente cercana a la organización.» «La municipalidad habría negado los fondos.»

topics.topic: Language contact: code-switching and loans
topics.notes: Spanish in contact with Limonese Creole English or Guaraní: switches, discourse particles (che, -na, luego), loanwords and what they signal about identity and audience. Code-switching between Spanish and Limonese Creole. «—Wa'appin, Lenny? —Todo bien, Miss Ivy, ¿y usted?» «Ella dijo “no carnival like before”, no “no carnival”.»

topics.topic: Literary -ra and pretérito anterior
topics.notes: -ra forms with pluperfect value in journalistic/literary prose (quien fuera alcalde, la que fuera su casa) and the pretérito anterior (apenas hubo terminado). Newspaper and memoir style. «Alfred King, quien fundara el Carnaval en 1949, decía que…» «Apenas hubo publicado la nota, empezaron las llamadas.»

c2-06.register: Newspaper (headline, lead, attribution, correction), radio call-in, Costa Rican colloquial, Limonese Creole.
c2-06.dialect: Costa Rican Spanish (usted even among friends, mae, diay, tuanis, pura vida) with Limonese Creole English (Mekatelyu) switches; Creole spellings to be checked with a Limonese speaker.
idioms: Comerse el cuento: to fall for a story
Echar más leña al fuego: to add fuel to the fire
El que mucho abarca poco aprieta: grasp all, lose all
Dar marcha atrás: to back-pedal
c2-06.vocabFocus: Journalism and carnival: el titular, la fuente, el desmentido, la rectificación, la exclusiva, viralizarse, la redacción, el editor, la cita textual, la comparsa, la carroza, el desfile, el calipso, el rice and beans, el pan bon, el patí, el ferrocarril, la bananera
facts: The Carnaval de Limón dates from 1949 and was founded by Alfred King (Alfred Henry Smith); it is held around 12 October, the date Columbus anchored off Limón in 1502 (Tico Times; Limón historians).
31 August is the Día de la Persona Negra y la Cultura Afrocostarricense (Ley 8938, 2011; August declared Mes Histórico de la Afrodescendencia by Ley 9526, 2018; holiday status by Ley 10050, 2021).
Jamaican and other Caribbean workers came to Limón from the 1870s to build the Atlantic railway and work on banana plantations (Costa Rican historiography).
Limonese Creole (Mekatelyu) is an English-lexifier creole spoken in Limón (linguistic descriptions).
A 2015 reform of Article 1 of the Constitution defines Costa Rica as multiethnic and pluricultural (Ley 9305; verify).

c2-07.title: Ndaje
c2-07.setting: A criminal court in Asunción and a sugar-cane farming area in Paraguarí department, Paraguay; present day.
c2-07.logline: Perla Benítez, 47, a sworn Guaraní–Spanish court interpreter in Asunción, is called in when the trial of Derlis Cañete, accused of setting fire to a neighbour's cane field, hinges on an elderly witness who speaks only Guaraní. The police translation says the witness 'saw' Derlis by the field, but in the recording Perla hears a small word the transcript left out: ndaje, 'so they say'. She must convince a sceptical prosecutor, Osmar Villalba, and the court that one particle separates a witness from a rumour, and then she traces the rumour back to the neighbour's own sugar-mill, where a spark started the fire.

topics.topic: Legal register and the future subjunctive
topics.notes: Legal-administrative formulas (por la presente, en virtud de, el abajo firmante) and the future subjunctive in statutes, contracts and proverbs (quien faltare, si así no lo hiciere, adonde fueres). Court formulas and the old-style warning read to witnesses. «Quien faltare a la verdad en su declaración incurrirá en falso testimonio.» «En virtud de lo dispuesto, se procede a la lectura del acta.»

topics.topic: Absolute constructions: terminada la audiencia
topics.notes: Participle (and gerund) clauses with their own subject for formal sequencing: leída el acta, firmado el acuerdo, una vez traducida la frase. Procedural sequencing. «Leída el acta, el juez concedió la palabra a la defensa.» «Terminada la audiencia, Perla se quedó sola con la grabación.» «Una vez traducida la frase, nadie dijo nada.»

topics.topic: Language contact: code-switching and loans
topics.notes: Spanish in contact with Limonese Creole English or Guaraní: switches, discourse particles (che, -na, luego), loanwords and what they signal about identity and audience. Paraguayan Spanish shaped by Guaraní. «—Che ra'a, ¿vos lo viste o te contaron?» «Vení-na un ratito.» «Mba'éichapa, ña Gumersinda.»

topics.topic: Marking the source: dizque, ndaje, había sido
topics.notes: Evidential strategies: hearsay dizque/dice que, Guaraní ndaje in Paraguayan Spanish, Andean mirative pluperfect (¡había sido verdad!), según parece. The whole plot turns on the source of knowledge. «Ndaje, dijo ella: “dicen que”.» «Dizque lo vieron con un bidón.» «Según parece, nadie lo vio realmente.»

c2-07.register: Courtroom Spanish and legal formulas, Perla's precise interpreter's notes, rural jopará dialogue.
c2-07.dialect: Paraguayan Spanish with voseo (vos sabés), Guaraní particles and loans (che 'my', -na softener, ña 'Mrs', mba'éichapa 'how are you'); Guaraní lines glossed and to be checked by a Guaraní speaker.
idioms: Hablar por boca de ganso: to repeat what others say
Cuando el río suena, piedras trae: there's no smoke without fire
Poner las manos en el fuego por alguien: to vouch for someone completely

facts: Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay alongside Spanish (Constitución Nacional 1992, art. 140; Ley de Lenguas 4251/2010).
Ndaje is a Guaraní reportative particle ('it is said'), also used in Paraguayan Spanish (linguistic literature, e.g., Döhla & Hennemann on ndaje).
Jopará is the everyday mixing of Guaraní and Spanish (Paraguayan sociolinguistics).
Paraguay uses oral, adversarial criminal trials under its Código Procesal Penal of 1998 (verify before citing details).

roleplay.register: formal usted, legal

c2-08.title: La última palabra de Ma Petrona
c2-08.setting: San Basilio de Palenque and Cartagena de Indias, Colombia; present day.
c2-08.logline: Dorina Salgado, 32, a linguist at a Cartagena university who grew up in San Basilio de Palenque, cannot stop thinking about the last word her grandmother Petrona said before she died, a Palenquero word nobody in the family recognises. She suspects a Kikongo root and asks a visiting Congolese linguist, Kiese Mbemba, for help, while her uncle Evaristo Cassiani, a respected member of his kuagro, insists the word is not for academics. The answer is social, not etymological: the word was the old name of Petrona's kuagro, a call to come back; Dorina understands that the message was for her and takes a post teaching Palenquero at the village school.

topics.notes: Future/conditional of conjecture woven into narration and their concessive use (será muy famoso, pero…; tendría razón, pero…), beyond B2's single-sentence conjecture. Questions and concessions. «¿Qué habrá querido decir?» «Tendría sus dudas, pero no las dijo.» «Será académica, pero sigue siendo nieta.»

topics.topic: Academic register: impersonal hedging
topics.notes: Impersonal, hedged academic prose (cabe señalar, se constata, los datos apuntan a, cabe la posibilidad de que + subjunctive) contrasted with the characters' speech. Dorina's draft paper versus her life. «Cabe la posibilidad de que se trate de un préstamo del kikongo.» «Los datos sugieren un uso restringido al ámbito del kuagro.»

c2-08.register: Academic abstract and field notes, Caribbean Colombian colloquial, short glossed Palenquero phrases.
c2-08.dialect: Caribbean Colombian Spanish (s-aspiration in the audio, ajá, ¿qué más?, vaina), tú and usted; Palenquero lexicon (moná, ma, kuagro, ngombe, lumbalú). All Palenquero lines to be checked by a Palenquero speaker or teacher.
idioms: El que nace pa' tamal, del cielo le caen las hojas (Caribbean Colombia): you can't escape your destiny
No hay peor sordo que el que no quiere oír: none so deaf as those who will not hear
Hablando se entiende la gente: talking things through solves problems
Volver por sus fueros: to return to one's old ways or rights
c2-08.vocabFocus: Language and community: la lengua criolla, el palenquero, el préstamo léxico, la etimología, la raíz, el sustrato, el kikongo, el hablante nativo, la revitalización, la etnoeducación, el kuagro, el lumbalú, el velorio, el cimarrón, el palenque, la grabación de campo, la transcripción, la glosa
facts: The cultural space of San Basilio de Palenque was proclaimed a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO in 2005 (inscribed on the Representative List in 2008) (UNESCO ICH).
Palenque was founded by cimarrones (maroons); its history is associated with the leader Benkos Biohó, whose statue stands in the plaza (Colombian historiography).
Palenquero is a Spanish-based creole with a Kikongo substrate; about 300 words of African origin are documented, including moná 'child', and the plural marker ma (Schwegler; Moñino & Schwegler 2002).
The kuagro (age-group organisation) and the lumbalú funeral ritual are central to Palenque's social life (UNESCO nomination file).
Palenquero is taught in the local school through ethno-education programmes (Colombian Ministry of Education; keep general).

roleplay.goal: Persuade him to share what he knows about the word, showing respect for community knowledge over academic curiosity.

c2-09.title: Lo que trajo el Crimea
c2-09.setting: Gijón (Cimadevilla), Asturias, Spain; 2019, with memories of 1937 (evacuation) and 1956 (return).
c2-09.logline: Covadonga Llaneza, 34, an ICU nurse in Gijón, inherits a box of cassette tapes from her great-aunt Nina, one of the 'children of Russia' evacuated to the Soviet Union in 1937, who returned in 1956 and never spoke about those twenty years. On one tape, between Asturian songs, a man's voice speaking Russian calls Nina 'mamochka', little mother, and the family's long silence turns into a question: did Nina leave a child behind? With a Russian-speaking colleague and the lists of the repatriation expeditions, Covadonga finds that 'Liosha' was an orphan Nina raised in a Soviet children's home; he is alive, 85, in Moscow, and the story ends with her phone call.

topics.topic: Free indirect speech
topics.notes: A character's thoughts rendered in third-person past narration without verbs of saying: questions, exclamations, deictics (mañana, aquí) and the character's own vocabulary inside the narrator's voice. Covadonga's thoughts merged with the narration. «¿Un hijo? ¿La tía Nina, que no dejaba que nadie le tocara la radio? No. Imposible. ¿O no?»

topics.topic: Diminutives and augmentatives: pragmatics
topics.notes: -ito/-ita, Andean -ito for politeness, Asturian -ín/-ina, -ón/-ota and -ucho for affection, irony, softening or contempt; the suffix as stance, not size. Three diminutive systems side by side. «—Ven, guapina, que te hago un cafetín.» (Asturian -ín/-ina) «Mamochka, decía la voz: mamaíta, madrecita.» «Una casina pequeña en Cimavilla.»

topics.topic: Por poco, por poco que
topics.notes: por poco + present indicative for a near miss in the past (por poco se me cae), por poco que + subjunctive (however little), con lo que + indicative (considering how much). Near misses in the search. «Por poco tira la caja de cintas al contenedor.» «Por poco que entendiera de ruso, aquella palabra la entendió.»

topics.topic: Literary -ra and pretérito anterior
topics.notes: -ra forms with pluperfect value in journalistic/literary prose (quien fuera alcalde, la que fuera su casa) and the pretérito anterior (apenas hubo terminado). Literary narration of the past. «La que fuera su casa durante veinte años estaba en las afueras de Moscú.» «Apenas hubo terminado la cinta, volvió a ponerla.»

c2-09.register: Literary narration with free indirect speech, 1950s documents and Red Cross-style lists, Asturian family dialogue (vosotros).
c2-09.dialect: Peninsular Spanish with vosotros and Asturian features: diminutive -ín/-ina, guaje (kid), me presta (I like it), chigre (bar), ho (vocative); Russian words glossed (mamochka, dacha).
idioms: Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente: what you don't know can't hurt you
Quien guarda, halla: waste not, want not
Agua pasada no mueve molino: let bygones be bygones
Cada casa es un mundo: every family is different
c2-09.vocabFocus: Exile, memory and recordings: la evacuación, el refugiado, la casa de niños, el exilio, la repatriación, el barco, el puerto, la cinta de casete, el magnetófono, la nana, la grabación, el huérfano, la transliteración, la sidrería, el escanciador, el chigre, la UCI, el expediente
facts: About 3,000 Spanish children were evacuated to the USSR in 1937–1938 during the Civil War, many from Asturias and the Basque Country (historiography of the 'niños de la guerra' / 'niños de Rusia').

Repatriation expeditions ran from 1956 to 1959, mostly aboard the ship Crimea to Valencia and Castellón (first arrival September 1956), the last to Almería in 1959; returnees included adults as well as former child evacuees (Cuadernos de Historia Contemporánea, 2016; regional studies).
Spanish evacuee children lived in Soviet 'casas de niños' (children's homes) (historiography).
The Asturian diminutive -ín/-ina is a regional feature in Asturian Spanish (dialectology).

roleplay.goal: Ask her about the tapes and help her decide whether, and how, to call Moscow.
roleplay.register: tú, Peninsular Spanish with Asturian warmth

c2-09.scene: Small flat in Cimadevilla with a view of the grey Cantabrian Sea: a woman in hospital scrubs wearing headphones beside an old cassette recorder, a cardboard box of tapes and black-and-white photos of children in coats on a ship's deck, a Soviet tea-glass holder on the table. Grey-blue sea, warm lamp yellow, faded sepia.
